header:
What difference does a **flat payment**
make on a credit card?

vo.text: Six thousand dollars on a card at 24%.
Pay the minimum: about eighteen years, and ten thousand in interest.
A flat $200 a month: under four years. About $7,200 less.
Just $20 more than the first minimum: fourteen years sooner.

verdict.text:
Just **$20** more than the first minimum:
**≈ 14 years** sooner

notes: Stress variant: 4 options, captions off (the label stack is the caption, HD Guy layout), long names, mixed duration units (years vs months share one bar scale), resultT/deltaT overrides on option 2. Maths: $6,000 at 24% APR (2% a month), no new charges, simulated month by month. Minimum = 1% of the balance + that month's interest, $35 floor: first payment $60 + $120 = $180; paid off after 219 payments (18.25 years ≈ 18.3), interest $10,441.80 ≈ $10,442. Flat $200: 47 payments, interest $3,254.63 ≈ $3,255 ($7,187.17 less; 219 − 47 = 172 months = 14.3 years sooner). Flat $300: 26 payments, $1,739.24 ($8,702.56 less). Flat $500: 14 payments, $929.90 ($9,511.90 less). $200 − $180 = $20 more than the first minimum.
